review_reference: Two migrations, applied in this order in one release: 0122 (Owner decision of 2026-11-10, relayed by Ola (clinical owner), for the Access PIN: "a PIN gives exactly 24 hours of read AND write access to all records, with no separate 'Ask for more access'", for the same staff roles as today (doctor, clinician, nurse: whoever holds identity.patient-access-pin.verify). From hid-system#208 (written as 0121, renumbered 0120) and #207 (apps/web), renumbered 0122 on 2026-11-17 because production now has 0001-0121 (0120 and 0121 are the outreach migrations).) and 0123 (Owner decision Q60 of 2026-11-12 ("build the QA tenant / use the mails we used for demo") and the coordinator's answers of the same day (three sides; QoreID, SMS and platform roles kept off; QA email limited to the owner's domain; Patient One pre-shared); to be signed by the owner; Rahman's review on hid-system#243: High 1 resolved by building 0123's PIN body on 0122's final body, Medium 2 recorded for #161, Low 3 closed at 4515c32e). Production has 0001-0121; its pending set after this branch is exactly 0122 and 0123. Unsigned: reviewed_by stays empty until the owner signs.
evidence: 0122: Migration 0122_patient_access_pin_day_read_write.sql (hid-system#208's file, renumbered from 0120). The SQL is #208's except its number: messages, temporary names, header and comments say 0122, the not-yet-applied precondition also requires 0121 (outreach.session_campaign_pairs() exists, else '0122: 0001-0121 must be applied first'), and the two comments inside the function body that named the migration say 0122, so the body md5 it pins is e17925c512f5f3e9fc79d84faded6ea1 (#208's was 60776067ac4f8fad8b34c7f25cb45a89). WHAT IT DOES: (a) access_requests_pin_scope_ck and consent_grants_pin_scope_ck (0033) allow read_records or write_records for a patient_access_pin row (still direct-care, never break-glass), dropped and added NOT VALID then validated; (b) CREATE OR REPLACE identity.access_patient_with_pin(text,text,integer) from 0098's body (md5 830c1baa4bca3df57cc02b7b002a8831 before, e17925c512f5f3e9fc79d84faded6ea1 after): every grant lasts exactly 1440 minutes whatever is asked (5-1440 still checked), request and grant are write_records, only a still-valid write_records PIN grant is reused, a deny of reading or writing (or every action) stops it, and the audit details and PatientAccessPinVerified payload carry scope; signature, result, owner, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path and ACL unchanged and compared after; (c) identity_outbox_minimum_necessary accepts the PIN notice with or without scope; (d) ALTER POLICY identity_outbox_patient_access_pin_insert admits a PIN grant of either scope and a payload scope equal to the grant's. No table, column, index, trigger, role, permission or grant change; 0122 itself leaves runtime-grants.sql as production has it (sha256 0da043d1f2ccba7e3c17af09772bea2da6f9d091e2986c9144a6c999d52fe9bf); the file is declared here for 0123's block; no row written. 0109-0121 change none of the objects 0122 reads or replaces (their md5 pins hold on 0001-0121). BACKWARD COMPATIBLE: identity-api reads the same result columns; today's image asks 15 or 5-60 and still works (the grant is write_records for 24 hours). The new identity-api in this branch defaults to 1440 and accepts 5-1440. The event dispatcher and notification worker already accept the three-key PIN notice (hid-system#206, live since 2026-11-11). apps/web (#207) asks 1440 and says 'see and add to records for 24 hours'. LOCKS: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on identity.access_requests, identity.consent_grants and identity.outbox_events until commit; behind another lock the runner stops after its 5 s lock_timeout with nothing applied. PROVED 2026-11-17 on throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 clusters (fictional data only, deleted afterwards), schema owned and migrated by a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS login (MIGRATION_TARGET=rds), runtime grants applied by the cluster superuser as security administrator: UPGRADE from this branch's 0001-0121 with production's runtime-grants.sql and the runtime-roles suite; plan exactly [0122] at the sha256 below; dry run rolled back (body still 830c1baa...); applied in about 140 ms; 0 pending; the file again answers '0122: already applied'; bootstrap and runtime-roles pass; body md5 e17925c512f5f3e9fc79d84faded6ea1. FRESH install of all 123 files: plan 123, dry run, apply, 0 pending, same md5. Database suites (94: 16 in database/tests, 78 in test/database): 92 pass on the upgraded and on the fresh database; schema.integration.sql and records-processing-draft.integration.sql fail there and fail the same way on 0001-0121 without 0122 (a NOBYPASSRLS schema owner; both pass, with all 94, when the schema owner is the cluster superuser as in scripts/run-container-database-acceptance.sh). On 0001-0121 without 0122 the six suites this change updates fail (patient-access-pin, patient-access-pin-actor-window, patient-grant-revocation, records-processing, sealed-demo-story, sealed-demo-tenant), so they test it. identity-api consent jest: 6 suites, 108 tests pass. Release checks: npm --prefix release test 98 of 98, npm --prefix release run verify and scripts/verify-migration-ledger.mjs pass. 0123: Migration 0123_sealed_qa_tenant.sql (hid-system#243's file, kept as 0123, rebuilt on live 0001-0122) plus its runtime-grants.sql block. WHAT IT DOES: a sealed QA tenant beside the real tenants and 0098's sealed demo, for the owner's own end-to-end testing; every QA login does every real action, and nothing crosses between the three sides (real, demo, QA). New owner-only table identity.sealed_qa_members (RLS enabled, not forced, one owner policy, no grant, immutable); helpers sealed_qa_ids, sealed_qa_facility (EXECUTE for hid_identity_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime, which the registration-read policy calls as the reader), sealed_qa_patient, sealed_qa_account, sealed_qa_recipient (the owner's domain @healthidentitydirectory.com, plus-addresses allowed) and the seed sealed_qa_install (owner only). SEAL: nine new BEFORE triggers beside 0098's, which keep their bodies: G1q consent grants and G2q staff memberships both QA or neither; G3q no platform role for a QA account; G4q a QA patient's share invitation to the owner's domain only and accepted on its side only; G5q no QA patient phone (no SMS); G6q no QoreID quota (no paid lookup); G7q a QA patient's emergency contact only an email the check recorded; G8q an outreach group whose organiser is a QA account is QA (name starting "QA "); G9q a QA outreach group invites the owner's domain only; and a member is never both demo and QA. Nine bodies replaced, each the live body byte for byte (md5-pinned in the preconditions: 0098's, measured equal on live 0001-0122 (0117-0121 replace none of them), and for access_patient_with_pin 0122's final body e17925c512f5f3e9fc79d84faded6ea1, so 0123 refuses to apply before 0122 ('0123: 0001-0122 must be applied first' while the body is still 0098's 830c1baa...); R3 is 0122's body byte for byte plus the one QA line, md5 6f44fc5433a8e2ddf1febbb711c88037 after) plus one QA clause beside its demo clause, always true for real and demo rows: create_access_request, activate_break_glass, access_patient_with_pin, ehr.send_order_route, search_order_destinations, search_share_providers, start_my_email_change, admin_platform_overview (QA not counted) and sealed_demo_contact_allowed (a QA branch before the demo branch, which is unchanged); identity.patients' policy patients_registration_read gets the same QA clause beside 0098's. DEMO PATIENT LOGINS MOVE (owner, 2026-11-12): patient1@ and patient2@ were 0098's demo patient logins, so in the same transaction, before the QA seed, demo_patient_logins_move (owner only) moves the two demo patient accounts to patientdemo1@ and patientdemo2@ (address, updated_at and row_version only; password, sessions, status, verification, Health IDs, shares and seal kept; one count-only audit row; refuses with 55000 a new address held by an account, staff record, open application or pending staff invitation, a demo login on neither address, or a demo patient's live email emergency contact or pending share invitation to an old address, so nothing of the demo still points at a QA mailbox; a second call moves nothing); 0098's exact allowlist sealed_demo_recipient and seed sealed_demo_install are replaced with the new addresses (md5-pinned before and after). SEED: on Amazon RDS only (rds_superuser), as 0098: QA Hospital, QA Laboratory, QA Pharmacy (the latter two with an approved admin_review application and product), seven staff logins (one mailbox of the owner's domain per role: ehr@, migrate@, lab@, lab2@, pharmacy@, admin@, outreach@) and two patient logins (patient1@, patient2@), pending_reset, no password, email verified; QA Patient One shares with the QA clinician at QA Hospital (grant, share row, a migration audit row); Health IDs HID-ZQAAAAA2 and HID-ZQAAAAA3. Refuses (55000, nothing written) when an address, id, slug, code, Health ID or CAC is held by someone else. Identity's generator never issues a code starting ZQA or ZDEM. KNOWN LIMITS (coordinator-accepted): no new login invited into QA and no new QA patient; QA Outreach is started by its organiser login through the normal flow. BACKWARD COMPATIBLE: real behaviour unchanged and demo behaviour unchanged but for the two demo patient addresses (every new clause is true for non-QA rows; the full sealed-demo suite passes; its pins of the eight bodies and records-processing's pin of create_access_request are updated to the new bodies). 0119's identity.outreach_health_id_registration calls identity.sealed_qa_facility(uuid) (boolean) by name when it exists, so from 0123 on a QA outreach group's registration gets no Health ID (42501 OUTREACH_HEALTH_ID_NOT_AVAILABLE), tested in the QA suite. For later migrations: hid-system#161 (not live) pins ehr.send_order_route at 0098's 4202ba3b... in prescription-dispensing-details and must pin 0123's 0c2def2b530bcb3d68537ade52787b6b instead (Rahman's Medium 2). LOCKS: SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE NOWAIT (5 s bound) on the ten tables that get a trigger, ACCESS EXCLUSIVE NOWAIT on identity.patients for the policy, last. TESTS: services/ehr-api/test/database/sealed-qa-tenant.integration.sql (structure, install and its refusals, every direction between real, demo and QA, the QA-only rules, the platform overview, the outreach group, overlap) and every existing database suite. PROOF OF 0122 AND 0123 TOGETHER: Proved 2026-11-17 on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster (fictional data only, deleted afterwards), schema owned and migrated by a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS login (MIGRATION_TARGET=rds), runtime grants applied by the cluster superuser as security administrator. Live bodies after 0001-0122 measured: the ten bodies 0123 replaces besides the PIN equal 0098's pins, the PIN equals 0122's e17925c5..., identity.patients has six policies and 0098's registration read. UPGRADE from 0001-0121 with production's runtime-grants.sql (sha256 0da043d1...) and the runtime-roles suite: plan exactly [0122, 0123]; dry run rolled back (PIN still 830c1baa...); applied (0122 17 ms, 0123 32 ms recorded); 0 pending; the 0123 file again answers '0123: already applied'; this branch's runtime-grants.sql and runtime-roles pass; PIN 6f44fc5433a8e2ddf1febbb711c88037. 0123 on 0001-0121 alone refuses '0123: 0001-0122 must be applied first'. FRESH install of all 124 files: plan, dry run, apply, 0 pending, same md5. services/ehr-api/scripts/test-staging-schema-upgrade.mjs against the local cluster passed: baseline 122 files, integrated 124, declared [0122, 0123], dry run rolled back, applied checksums preserved, migration grants match runtime-grants.sql (2624), clean install, row security of 205 tables unchanged, the no-FORCE control-settings baseline released the same way. Database suites (95: 16 in database/tests, 79 in test/database, with sealed-qa-tenant): 93 pass on the upgraded and on the fresh database; schema.integration.sql and records-processing-draft.integration.sql fail there exactly as on 0001-0121 (a NOBYPASSRLS schema owner); all 95 pass when the schema owner is the cluster superuser. AMAZON RDS PATH simulated with a role named rds_superuser: 0001-0122 with 0098's demo seed and 0102's story (after the demo logins' password reset and the controls as production has them); the four read-only pre-sign queries in 0123's header answered as the header requires (query 1 every count 0 for all eleven addresses; query 2 exactly the two demo logins, demo t, patient1@ and patient2@, active, 0 own_email, 0 email_contacts, 0 old_address_invitations; query 3 health_ids 0, facility_codes 0, rds 1; query 4 information only); then 0123 applied with the move and the seed inside the migration: the demo logins at patientdemo1@ and patientdemo2@ (still active, password kept), nine QA logins pending_reset with no password and a verified address, QA Hospital, QA Laboratory and QA Pharmacy, HID-ZQAAAAA2 and HID-ZQAAAAA3, one seeded share, three count-only audit rows; a second sealed_qa_install() inserted 0. identity-api jest (hid-code-generator, emergency-contact, consent): 9 suites, 186 tests pass. npm --prefix release test 98 of 98, release verify and scripts/verify-migration-ledger.mjs (124 migrations) pass.
